backlog.spec: The starter has three defects: construct_packing returns two values while run_packing unpacks three, compute_max_radii has a nested loop that re-binds i and j and makes the pair pass wrong, and the initial clip to [0.01, 0.99] is ad hoc. Rewrite construct_packing to return (centers, radii, sum_radii) and compute_max_radii as a single correct pass over unordered pairs that takes the min of border distance and half-distance-minus-margin. Keep a 1e-9 safety shrink so the double-precision check passes with zero tolerance.
backlog.title: Fix the broken starter scaffolding first

backlog.spec: Keep the 26 centers fixed and solve for the radii that maximise sum(r) subject to r_i <= x_i, r_i <= 1 - x_i, r_i <= y_i, r_i <= 1 - y_i, and r_i + r_j <= ||c_i - c_j|| for all pairs. Use scipy.optimize.linprog with the highest-accuracy method and then shrink every radius by 1e-10 before returning. This converts any center layout into its best variable-radius packing and is the inner step for every other idea.
backlog.title: Exact max-radii LP given fixed centers

backlog.spec: Build the decision vector z = [x_1..x_26, y_1..y_26, r_1..r_26] and maximise sum(r) with scipy.optimize.minimize method SLSQP. Constraints are the border constraints r_i <= x_i, r_i <= 1-x_i (and same for y), plus pairwise r_i + r_j <= dist(c_i,c_j) written in squared form for smoothness. Start from a hexagonal-ish grid of centers with radii 0.08, bound all variables to [0,1] and [0,0.5], and cap maxiter near 300 so the run fits in 4 minutes.
backlog.title: Joint SLSQP over centers and radii

backlog.spec: Optimise unconstrained variables (centers and radii) using L-BFGS-B on the objective -sum(r) plus a quadratic penalty mu * (sum of squared positive overlaps + sum of squared border violations). Start mu at 10 and multiply by 10 each stage for about 6 stages, warm-starting each stage from the previous solution. At the end, run the exact LP radius step on the final centers so the output is strictly feasible.
backlog.title: Penalty continuation with L-BFGS

backlog.spec: Use np.random.default_rng(12345) to generate K random initial center sets (uniform in [0.05,0.95]^2) and for each run a short penalty-based relaxation followed by the exact LP radius step. Keep the packing with the largest sum of radii. Choose K so the whole loop finishes in about 200 seconds by timing the first start and stopping when the budget is near exhaustion.
backlog.title: Multi-start from random seeded layouts

backlog.spec: Start from the best packing found so far. Repeat: perturb a random subset of 2 to 4 centers by Gaussian noise of scale 0.05 to 0.15, re-optimise with the penalty plus LP pipeline, and accept the new layout if its sum of radii exceeds the current one (with a small probability otherwise, Metropolis style at temperature 0.002). Use a fixed seed and stop at a wall-clock limit of 200 seconds.
backlog.title: Basin hopping on the best packing

backlog.spec: Represent a packing by its 26 centers only. At each step propose moving one random center by a Gaussian step whose scale decays geometrically from 0.1 to 0.001 over the run. Score each proposal by the exact LP max-radii sum (or a fast greedy radius computation using vectorised numpy pair distances). Accept with the Metropolis rule with temperature decaying from 0.01 to 1e-5. Track and return the best state seen.
backlog.title: Simulated annealing on center positions

backlog.spec: Replace the pairwise Python loops with numpy broadcasting: compute the full 26x26 distance matrix once, and for a given center set compute radii by a greedy pass that sorts circles by their border distance and assigns each the largest radius feasible against already-assigned neighbours and borders. This gives a cheap approximate score for many layouts and is meant to feed search loops that call it thousands of times.
backlog.title: Vectorised greedy radius computation for fast scoring

backlog.spec: Generate a hex-like lattice of about 30 candidate points covering the unit square with spacing chosen so the lattice has roughly 26 points inside [0.05,0.95]^2, then keep the 26 points that best fit the square (for example, drop the points nearest the border corners first). Feed these centers into the LP radius step to get an initial value, and then refine with a penalty relaxation. The goal is to exploit the dense hexagonal core while letting edge circles adapt.
backlog.title: Start from a hexagonal lattice with edge adjustments

backlog.spec: Initialise a layout with a few large circles near the centre and progressively smaller circles toward the border, by placing centers on concentric rings with ring radius decreasing outward and assigning initial radii that decrease with ring index. Then optimise the joint variables with the penalty method and finish with the exact LP step. This targets the mixed-size structure that tends to beat equal-size packings for the sum-of-radii objective.
backlog.title: Mixed-size initialisation: large center, small rim

backlog.spec: Force four circles into the square corners with radius near the corner distance and place several circles along each edge at evenly spaced positions, with the remaining interior circles placed at random. Run the penalty plus LP pipeline from this seed. Boundary circles are frequently active constraints in good packings, so pinning a few of them to the walls as a starting structure can speed convergence to a strong local optimum.
backlog.title: Corner and edge seeding

backlog.spec: Restrict the search to layouts symmetric under reflection about the diagonal x = y, or about the vertical axis x = 0.5. Parameterise only the independent half of the centers (about 13 free centers, with mirror images generated automatically) and optimise over those with the penalty plus LP pipeline. Symmetry halves the dimension and often finds high-quality packings quickly; then run a final unconstrained polish on all 26 centers.
backlog.title: Symmetric search under reflection

backlog.spec: Use a smooth overlap penalty based on softplus of (r_i + r_j - d_ij) with a temperature parameter beta that starts at 5 and grows to 500 over the optimisation, computed with analytic gradients. Iterate L-BFGS-B at each beta value. Early small beta lets circles pass through each other and find a good global arrangement; large beta enforces feasibility. Finish with the exact LP radius step on the resulting centers.
backlog.title: Soft-to-hard overlap penalty schedule

backlog.spec: Write the penalty objective and its exact gradient with respect to all centers and radii in vectorised numpy, using the pair mask i<j from np.triu_indices. Pass the gradient to scipy.optimize.minimize (L-BFGS-B) so that finite-difference noise is removed. This should make each local solve several times faster and allow more restarts or basin-hopping steps within the 4-minute budget.
backlog.title: Analytic gradients for the penalty objective

backlog.spec: In the iterative relaxation, maintain a trust-region radius on the center displacement. After each step compare the predicted and actual improvement of the penalised objective, expand the region by a factor of 1.5 when the ratio is above 0.75, and shrink it by 0.5 when the ratio is below 0.25. Stop when the region falls below 1e-7 or the wall-clock budget is hit. This avoids oscillation when many circles are close to contact.
backlog.title: Adaptive step size with trust region

backlog.spec: Treat each circle as a particle with a radius that grows while it is not in contact. At each iteration, compute repulsive forces from overlapping neighbours and from the walls, move each center along the net force by a small step, and increase each radius by a small amount proportional to the free space it has. Once the growth stalls, freeze the radii and apply the exact LP step. This is a physics-style inflation method suited to finding jammed packings.
backlog.title: Repulsion-based relaxation with radius growth

backlog.spec: Alternate between assigning each square sample point to its nearest circle center weighted by current radius (a power diagram with weights r_i squared) and moving each center to the centroid of its assigned sample points. Use a fixed grid of about 40000 sample points for the assignment. Update radii from the LP step after each sweep. Repeat for a fixed number of sweeps from several random starts and keep the best.
backlog.title: Lloyd-style centroid relaxation

backlog.spec: Build the packing incrementally: start with an empty square, and repeatedly add the circle at the point that maximises the radius it can take given existing circles (sample candidate points on a fine grid, compute the feasible radius with a vectorised distance to borders and existing circles). After 26 placements, run a removal-and-reinsert loop that takes out the smallest circle and tries to reinsert it at the best free spot, keeping improvements. Finish with the LP step.
backlog.title: Greedy insertion with removal

backlog.spec: Maintain a population of about 12 packings drawn from random seeds and run the penalty plus LP pipeline on each. Each generation, create children by taking the centers in the left half of one parent and the right half of another, repairing any duplicates by moving the nearest center, and locally optimising. Replace the worst members when a child is better. Use a fixed seed and a wall-clock limit. This explores diverse basins more systematically than independent restarts.
backlog.title: Population-based search with recombination

backlog.spec: At each iteration generate a batch of 32 candidate perturbations of the current best center set, stack them into one numpy array of shape (32, 26, 2), and compute all their pairwise distance tensors and border constraints at once. Pick the candidate with the best greedy radius sum and continue from it. This amortises Python overhead across candidates and gives a much higher evaluation rate for the search loops.
backlog.title: Batch-parallel evaluation of perturbations

backlog.spec: During relaxation, at each step only optimise a random subset of about 8 circles (chosen with a fixed-seed generator) while the others are held fixed, cycling through subsets across iterations. Each subset solve is a small penalty problem that is cheap to run. After several full cycles, run a final joint optimisation on all variables and the LP step. Coordinate-block descent of this kind can escape local jams that the full solve gets stuck in.
backlog.title: Minibatch-style random subset relaxation

backlog.spec: Add a small quadratic regulariser lambda * ||centers - template||^2 to the penalty objective, where template is a good structured layout (such as the best hex-grid guess). Decay lambda from 0.1 to 0 across the stages so the optimiser is nudged toward the template early and then free to deviate. Keep the regulariser out of the final stage so the result reflects the true objective, and finish with the LP step.
backlog.title: Overlap penalty with L2 regularisation toward a template

backlog.spec: Add a small penalty that discourages extreme radius disparity, for example a term epsilon * sum((r_i - mean r)^2) with epsilon of 1e-3 that is removed in the final stage. The intent is to keep the optimiser from collapsing many circles to zero radius early on, which happens with poor starting layouts. Enforce r_i >= 0 with bounds and finish with the exact LP radius step on the final centers.
backlog.title: Radius cap and minimum-radius regularisation

backlog.spec: After any optimisation, run a repair pass that computes all pairwise and border violations in double precision and scales the offending radii down until every constraint holds with strict inequality. Then multiply all radii by (1 - 1e-9) as a final safety margin. Verify with an explicit check that every center lies in [0,1]^2 and that no pair overlaps before returning, so the harness never sees an invalid packing.
backlog.title: Safety margin and feasibility repair

backlog.spec: Wrap the whole pipeline in a controller that tracks elapsed time with time.perf_counter and reserves a fixed margin (about 40 seconds) before the 5-minute cap. It allocates budget across stages (seeding, relaxation, LP polish, basin hopping) based on how long each stage took, and stops early if the best sum of radii has not improved over the last several iterations. This keeps the run within the harness limit while spending most time on the most productive stage.
backlog.title: Time-budgeted adaptive search controller

backlog.spec: Phase one runs a coarse global search: many short penalty relaxations from random seeds with a soft overlap penalty, keeping the top five packings. Phase two takes each of those five and runs a tight local refinement with a stiff penalty and the joint SLSQP solve, followed by the exact LP step. Return the best refined result. The separation of exploration from exploitation mirrors standard practice in packing research.
backlog.title: Two-phase global then local refinement

backlog.spec: Start from a dense square or hexagonal grid of 26 points in the square, then apply a sequence of discrete moves: remove one circle from a random position and reinsert it at the largest empty hole found by sampling a grid, or shift a row by half a spacing to create a dislocation. After each move, run the LP radius step to score it, and keep moves that increase the sum. This explores structured defects in the lattice rather than continuous noise.
backlog.title: Lattice perturbation with dislocation moves

backlog.spec: After _lp_radii solves the max-radii LP, read the dual values (res.ineqlin.marginals) of the pair and wall constraints. Pairs with a large dual are the binding contacts that limit the total radius. Compute, for each circle, the gradient of the sum of radii with respect to its center by summing dual-weighted unit vectors over its active pair constraints. Take a small step along the gradient of the best-scoring candidate, rescore with the LP, and keep the step only if the sum improves. Use this as an extra move type in the basin-hopping loop, sampled with probability 0.3, with a fixed seed.
backlog.title: LP-dual sensitivity move for center updates

backlog.spec: After each local optimisation, identify rattlers: circles with no active pair or wall constraint whose LP radius is set by a loose bound, or whose slack exceeds 1e-6. Build the contact graph from constraints with slack below 1e-7. Pick one rattler at random and move it to the grid point with the largest free hole, computed as min(distance to other centers minus their radii, 2 times wall distance). Relax with _relax and re-score, accepting only if the sum improves. This replaces the random reinsertion with a targeted move.
backlog.title: Rattler relocation via contact graph

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that picks one circle among the largest-radius third and one among the smallest-radius third of the current best packing, swaps their centers, then runs _relax for 150 steps with the current centers as template and _slsqp_refine with 80 iterations before scoring. The swap moves big circles into different positions while leaving the total number of circles unchanged. Use a fixed seed and only accept improvements over the current state.
backlog.title: Large-small center swap move

backlog.spec: Add a perturbation move that applies a global transform to all centers of the current best packing: scale the coordinates about the square center by a factor drawn uniformly from [0.93, 1.07], then add a small per-axis shift in [-0.02, 0.02]. Clip to [0,1], relax with _relax for 200 steps, run _slsqp_refine, and score. This changes the whole basin at once rather than moving a few circles, so it explores a different family of contact graphs. Use a fixed seed and keep it as one of the move types in the existing loop.
backlog.title: Global affine squeeze-and-expand perturbation

backlog.spec: Keep a tabu list of circle indices moved in the last 10 accepted or rejected basin-hopping iterations. When choosing which circles to perturb, sample only from circles not on the tabu list, and push each newly perturbed index onto the list with a FIFO of length 10. This stops the loop from repeatedly disturbing the same two or three circles, spreading perturbations across the packing. Keep the fixed seed and the existing acceptance rule.
backlog.title: Tabu memory on recently moved circles

backlog.spec: Wrap _score in a dictionary cache keyed on the candidate center array rounded to 6 decimals, converted to bytes. Before calling the LP, check the cache; return the stored (radii, sum) on a hit. Repeated near-identical candidates from the reinsertion and perturbation moves then cost nothing, so the fixed time budget covers more distinct iterations. Clear the cache at the start of construct_packing. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged.
backlog.title: Memoised evaluation cache for candidate centers

backlog.spec: Run three independent basin-hopping chains in an interleaved loop, each with its own fixed seed (for example 7, 11, 19) and its own current state started from different members of the coarse population. Every 40 iterations, copy the best state into the worst chain so good basins spread while the others keep diversity. Return the best state over all chains. The time budget is split evenly among chains, checked against the same wall clock limit as before.
backlog.title: Island model with periodic migration

backlog.spec: After the search finishes, generate the 8 dihedral images of the best center set under the square's symmetry group (x to 1-x, y to 1-y, and swapping x and y). For each image, run _relax for 300 steps and _slsqp_refine with 120 iterations, then score it with _score. Return the image with the highest valid sum. Symmetric transforms do not change the packing sum, but the relaxation starts from a different numerical point and can reach a slightly better local optimum.
backlog.title: Symmetry-image polish of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Track the number of consecutive basin-hopping iterations without improvement. After 60 such iterations, reset the current state to a randomly selected member of the top-5 coarse population, which is kept in a list, and resume the loop. The global best is never reset. Keep the fixed seed. This is a discrete restart schedule that escapes deep local optima without discarding the best solution found so far.
backlog.title: Stagnation restart from the elite pool

backlog.spec: Adapt the perturbation scale of the basin-hopping Gaussian move with the one-fifth success rule. Keep a rolling window of the last 20 iterations and count how many produced an accepted improvement. If the success fraction is above 0.2, multiply the perturbation scale by 1.1; if below 0.2, multiply it by 0.9. Clamp the scale to [0.005, 0.2]. Start from the current scale of 0.05 to 0.15 mid-range. The step adapts to the landscape instead of being drawn from a fixed interval, with a fixed seed kept for repeatability.
backlog.title: One-fifth success rule for perturbation size

backlog.spec: Before the main search, run a short search for a 25-circle packing and a 27-circle packing using the existing pipeline with a reduced time budget. Derive a 26-circle start by deleting the circle with the smallest LP radius from the 27-circle packing, and by inserting one circle at the largest hole (grid-sampled, as in the basin-hopping move) into the 25-circle packing. Add both starts to the coarse-phase population, scored with the existing LP scorer, so the population mixes transferred and random candidates. Keep all seeds fixed and keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Hierarchical n±1 transfer from neighbouring packings

backlog.spec: Replace the single-chain basin-hopping loop in construct_packing with K=4 replica chains at a fixed geometric temperature ladder (for example T from 0.0005 to 0.005). Each replica runs the existing perturb, relax, SLSQP, LP-score step. After every block of about 20 steps, propose swaps between adjacent temperatures using the Metropolis criterion on the LP sums, and keep a global best across all replicas. Use a fixed seed and keep the wall-clock guard so the total stays under about 215 s.
backlog.title: Parallel tempering over the incumbent basin

backlog.spec: After _slsqp_refine, run scipy.optimize.minimize with method='trust-constr' on the same joint problem (maximise sum of radii, pair and wall inequality constraints, with analytic Jacobians for the constraint function), starting from the refined point and limited to about 300 iterations. Accept the trust-constr result only if _score on its centers gives a larger valid sum than the SLSQP result. Wrap the call in try/except and fall back to the SLSQP result. This is a different local solver from SLSQP, so it may find a slightly different local optimum.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of the joint centers-and-radii problem

backlog.spec: After the final LP, identify the active contacts: pairs with gap below 1e-7 and walls with radius within 1e-7 of the boundary. Form the nonlinear system of equalities (pair distance equals sum of radii, wall distance equals radius) in the unknowns (centers, radii) for these active constraints. Solve it with a few damped Gauss-Newton steps (least squares via numpy.linalg.lstsq on the Jacobian). Accept the new point only if the LP-scored valid sum improves, and then run _make_valid to restore strict feasibility with the margin. This snaps the packing onto its exact contact structure.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton (KKT) exact polish

backlog.spec: In the coarse phase and in the basin-hopping loop, screen candidates in rounds. Round 1 runs _relax with only 60 steps and scores with the LP. Keep the best 25 percent of candidates, run _relax with 200 steps, and keep the best 25 percent of those. Only the final survivors receive the full _slsqp_refine and LP score. The budget per round is fixed, so more starts fit into the 4-minute limit. Keep all seeds fixed.
backlog.title: Multi-fidelity successive halving for candidate screening

backlog.spec: Replace the random Gaussian center perturbations in the basin-hopping stage with a simple (mu, lambda) evolution strategy over the 52-dimensional center vector. Use lambda=12 offspring per generation sampled from N(mean, sigma^2 C), where C is a rank-mu covariance update from the top third of offspring. Score each offspring by _relax (short steps) followed by _score. Update the mean to the weighted best offspring, and adapt sigma with a one-fifth-style rule. Restart the search from the incumbent with fixed seeds.
backlog.title: CMA-ES style covariance-adapted center search

backlog.spec: Add a deterministic sweep stage after _two_phase. For each circle in turn, try a fixed set of 24 displacement directions (8 directions at 3 radii, about 0.01, 0.03, 0.08) and the 49-point grid of hole positions. For each candidate position, compute the LP-scored valid sum with the other centers fixed, and move the circle only if the sum rises. Repeat the sweep until no circle moves or the time budget is reached. This is an exact, derivative-free local search over single-circle moves.
backlog.title: Coordinate-wise exact line search with LP scoring

backlog.spec: In _slsqp_refine, add a regulariser to the objective: minus sum of radii minus lam times the sum of squared deviations of radii from their mean, with lam set to 0.05 at the start of each call and annealed linearly to 0 over the SLSQP iterations (implement by running the SLSQP call in three stages with lam = 0.05, 0.02, 0). The bonus encourages the solver to leave the symmetric equal-radius basin before the final stage removes it. The final stage uses the pure sum-of-radii objective, so the returned value is judged by the unregularised LP score.
backlog.title: Radius-spread regularised SLSQP with annealed bonus

backlog.spec: Change the initial radii used by _relax in the coarse phase from a constant 0.005 to values drawn from a log-uniform distribution on [0.02, 0.12] with the fixed seed. Half of the population members receive a size prior: 3 to 5 circles get initial radius about 0.12 to 0.15 and the rest get about 0.06, placed at random. The relaxation then grows radii into free space, so the population covers a wider range of size distributions than the uniform start, which the LP scorer then ranks.
backlog.title: Log-uniform initial radii and size-prior starts

backlog.spec: Run the two-phase search with three different fixed seeds (for example 2024, 31, 977), each with one third of the coarse-phase time budget, and keep the best five candidates from each seed (fifteen in total) for the shared refinement stage. The refinement stage uses the existing relax, SLSQP and LP scoring, with the same per-candidate time guard. Basin hopping then runs from the single best refined packing. The portfolio reduces dependence on one random start, and the seeds are fixed so results stay repeatable.
backlog.title: Multi-seed portfolio with time-sliced selection

backlog.spec: Replace the random starts in _two_phase with a deterministic-seeded Riesz energy minimisation. For each start, minimise E(c) = sum over pairs of 1/d_ij^s plus a wall term, using L-BFGS (analytic gradient, with wall penalty 1/(x^s) type barriers on each side). Anneal the exponent s through the schedule 2, 6, 12, 24, 48, using the previous stage's minimiser as the next start, so the points spread out like a max-min-distance (Tammes-style) configuration. Then pass the result through the existing _relax, _slsqp_refine and _score pipeline unchanged. Use the Riesz outputs as the population seeds for the coarse phase.
backlog.title: Riesz-energy spreading continuation

backlog.spec: Add a constructor that searches only over packings invariant under a 180-degree rotation about (0.5, 0.5). Use 13 free centres p_k and set the other 13 to (1 - x, 1 - y). Run relaxation and LP scoring on the reduced 26-dimensional variable, with pair and wall constraints taken on the full 26-circle set (mirror images contribute constraints too). Keep the best 3 symmetric results, then release the symmetry and run _relax and _slsqp_refine on the full 26 centres to polish them. Feed the best polished result into the basin-hopping stage as its starting point. Seed fixed.
backlog.title: 180-degree rotationally symmetric search

backlog.spec: Build a 27-circle packing with the existing two-phase pipeline (set _N to 27 for that stage only). For every circle k, remove it, compute the exact LP radii for the remaining 26 centres using _lp_radii and _make_valid, and keep the removal that gives the largest sum. Then run _relax with the template argument set to the current 26 centres, followed by _slsqp_refine and _score on the 26-circle set. Also try the 3 best removals and keep the best final result. This hierarchical n+1 to n transfer gives a different basin family from building up from 26 directly.
backlog.title: Delete-one-from-27 construction

backlog.spec: Add a fixed-seed differential evolution (DE/rand/1/bin, F=0.6, CR=0.9) stage over the 52-dimensional vector of all centres, with a population of 30 candidates initialised from the current elite pool plus random perturbations. Fitness is the exact LP sum from _score, with None mapped to -1. Vectorise the trial generation with numpy, clip trials to [0,1], and run generations until 90 seconds of wall time have passed. Feed the best member into the existing _slsqp_refine and _score steps. This is a derivative-free global search that differs from the current gradient-based relaxation.
backlog.title: Differential evolution over centre vectors

backlog.spec: Replace the penalty continuation with a log-barrier method that keeps every iterate strictly feasible. Maximise F(z) = sum r_i + mu * [sum over pairs log(d_ij - r_i - r_j) + sum over walls log(x_i - r_i) and the other three wall gaps], where z is the joint centres-and-radii vector. Start from a feasible configuration (the _make_valid output with a 1e-3 shrink). Use gradient ascent with backtracking line search that rejects any step leaving the feasible set. Decrease mu by a factor of 0.3 from 1e-2 down to 1e-7 over about 8 stages, running 30 iterations per stage. Finish with _score to get the exact LP radii.
backlog.title: Log-barrier feasible interior path

backlog.spec: Add an event-free molecular-dynamics growth stage. Start with the 26 centres at random positions and radii of 0 with random velocities. At each time step, move the centres by velocity times dt, reflect them off the walls, and grow every radius at a rate of g = 0.002 per unit time. When any pair gap d_ij - r_i - r_j becomes negative, the two circles are pushed apart along their line of centres with an elastic bounce (exchange normal velocity components, scaled by 0.9 restitution) and their radii are capped at half the gap. Run for a fixed number of steps (about 4000) with a fixed seed, then feed the centres to _relax, _slsqp_refine and _score. Keep the result as a new population member.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-Stillinger style growth

backlog.spec: Build a starting packing from a prescribed radius profile rather than from random centres. Set target radii as a decreasing function of distance to the square's centre (for example one large circle of radius 0.12 at the centre and smaller ones outward, drawn from a seeded log-uniform spread). Generate a dense pool of 200 candidate sites from a jittered grid. Use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on a cost matrix that penalises placing a large target radius at a site near a wall (cost equals target radius minus distance to nearest wall) to assign the 26 target radii to 26 chosen sites. Then run _relax with these fixed radii as initial values, followed by _slsqp_refine and _score. Add this as a population seed in the coarse phase.
backlog.title: Prescribed radius profile with Hungarian slot assignment

backlog.spec: Add a fixed-seed cross-entropy method stage. Maintain a Gaussian per circle (mean and standard deviation for x and y, initialised from the current incumbent with a sigma of 0.05). In each of 12 iterations, sample 40 full centre sets from these Gaussians, clip them to [0,1], and score each with _relax (short schedule) followed by _score. Take the top 8 samples by LP sum as the elite set. Refit each circle's mean and sigma to its elite positions, with sigma floored at 0.002, and blend the update with the previous parameters using a rate of 0.7. After the final iteration, run _slsqp_refine on the best elite and keep it if it beats the incumbent.
backlog.title: Cross-entropy method over centre distributions

backlog.spec: Replace uniform random centre initialisation in _two_phase with a deterministic low-discrepancy sequence. Generate 2000 points with a base-2 and base-3 Halton sequence in the square, then choose the 26 centres greedily by farthest-point sampling: start from the point nearest the centre, and repeatedly add the candidate that maximises its minimum distance to the chosen set, with wall distances folded in as twice the wall distance. Use this set as the first start, and perturb it with seeded Gaussian noise of standard deviation 0.01 to produce the remaining population members. Everything downstream stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Quasi-random Halton seeding with farthest-point greedy

backlog.spec: Wrap the acceptance rule of the basin-hopping loop with a stochastic tunnelling transform. Define the transformed score as h(s) = 1 - exp(-gamma * (s - s_ref)) where s is the LP sum of a candidate and s_ref is the current incumbent sum minus 0.002. Use gamma = 40 and accept or reject candidates by a Metropolis test on h rather than on s. This flattens the high-scoring basin and lowers the barrier between nearby packings, so the search can cross low-scoring ridges. Keep the best raw-score packing as the output, and keep the rest of the loop unchanged, with the seed fixed.
backlog.title: Stochastic tunnelling on the LP objective

backlog.spec: Add a search mode that restricts centers to be symmetric under reflection across the diagonal y = x. Sample 13 free centers (fixed seed) and set their mirror images to (y, x). Circles lying on the diagonal (where x and y are equal) are allowed as one-dimensional free points. Relax and run SLSQP/LP on the full 26-circle set, then release the symmetry constraint and refine the best symmetric result without it. Keep the best valid packing. Do not reuse the x=0.5 mirror or the 180-degree rotation, which have already been tried.
backlog.title: Diagonal-reflection symmetric search

backlog.spec: Before the wall-constrained relaxation, run a short relaxation on a torus of side 1 where pair distances use the minimum-image convention and there are no walls. This spreads the circles without boundary artefacts. Then map the centers into the square by a fixed affine rescale, and run the existing wall-aware relaxation and LP scoring from that start. Use a fixed seed and a few starting configurations, and keep the best valid result.
backlog.title: Periodic-torus relaxation then unwrap

backlog.spec: Run the relaxation inside an inner box [m, 1-m] for each circle center, where the margin m is annealed from 0.12 down to 0 over the steps. Wall forces and the LP are then applied to the true unit square. At each stage the centers stay inside the inner box, which spreads the configuration early and lets it fill the corners as the margin relaxes. Use a fixed seed and apply the existing SLSQP and LP scoring at the end.
backlog.title: Shrinking-box continuation

backlog.spec: Around the current incumbent, draw a batch of 60 random perturbation vectors (fixed seed, scale chosen by an adaptive rule). Evaluate each perturbation with the existing LP score. Fit a quadratic regression of the score on the flattened perturbation (52 coordinates) with a small ridge term. Then take the surrogate's maximiser within a trust-region ball, evaluate it exactly with the LP, and accept it only if the true score improves. Repeat for a fixed number of rounds.
backlog.title: Quadratic surrogate of the LP score

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP call, compute the Delaunay triangulation of the current centers (scipy.spatial.Delaunay). Keep only pair constraints for triangulation edges plus any pair closer than the current radii sum plus 0.05. Pass this reduced constraint set to the joint centers-and-radii SLSQP, which avoids the full 325-pair set and speeds each call. After the solve, check all pairs with the exact validity routine, so no infeasible pair is accepted. Use the saved time to run more basin-hopping steps.
backlog.title: Delaunay-locked constraint set for SLSQP

backlog.spec: In the relaxation, replace the hard overlap maximum with a log-sum-exp soft penalty over all pair and wall gaps, with sharpness beta annealed from 5 to 200 across the steps. Gradients are analytic. The radii are updated by the soft minimum of the gaps. This gives a smooth landscape early and a near-exact constraint at the end. Keep the LP and SLSQP scoring unchanged, and select the best valid packing.
backlog.title: Log-sum-exp smooth objective with annealed sharpness

backlog.spec: In the coarse population, cross two parents by running k-means (k=2, fixed seed) on the union of their centers. Take the cluster of parent A that lies in one half-plane and the cluster of parent B that lies in the other, then match by nearest neighbour to reach 26 circles. Fill any gap with circles placed at the largest holes found on a 40 by 40 grid. Relax the child, score it with the LP, and replace the worst population member if the child is better. Use a fixed seed throughout.
backlog.title: Voronoi-cluster crossover of population members

backlog.spec: Partition the 26 centers into 3 to 5 spatial clusters with k-means (fixed seed) at each perturbation. Move each cluster as a rigid body, applying a random rotation of up to 10 degrees and a translation of up to 0.03 about the cluster centroid. Clip to the square, relax briefly with the existing relaxation, then run the joint SLSQP and LP scoring. Accept with the existing Metropolis rule on the sum of radii. This explores collective motions that single-circle moves cannot reach.
backlog.title: Rigid cluster moves on the contact graph

backlog.spec: Starting from the incumbent, run a gradient-free Hooke-Jeeves pattern search over the 52 center coordinates. The objective is the exact LP sum of radii after _make_valid. Each exploratory move steps one coordinate by plus or minus a step h, keeping the step only if the score rises. After a full sweep with no gain, halve h. Continue until h falls below 1e-4 or the time budget is reached. Use the LP score as the only objective, with no penalty terms, and keep the best valid packing.
backlog.title: Hooke-Jeeves pattern search on the LP objective

backlog.spec: Start from a radius profile with a few large circles and many small ones. Prescribe 6 large radii near 0.17 and 20 small radii near 0.09 as an initial radius vector. Sample the initial centers by a farthest-point greedy rule (fixed seed) with the large slots first. Relax the centers with the radii held fixed, then run the joint SLSQP and LP scoring with the radii free. Keep the best of several seeded profiles, scored by the exact LP.
backlog.title: Two-tier radius-class assignment with fixed slots

backlog.spec: Replace the random-restart stage of _two_phase (or add a stage after it) with scipy.optimize.dual_annealing over the 52-dimensional center vector bounded to [0.05, 0.95]^2. The objective is -sum(_score(c)) with _score returning -1 on LP failure, seeded with a fixed seed (e.g. 4242), maxiter set so the stage stops by about 120 s wall time via a callback that returns True when the clock is exceeded. Feed the best center set into the existing _relax and _slsqp_refine polish before the final _make_valid. Keep the rest of construct_packing unchanged.
backlog.title: Dual annealing over center vectors with LP scoring

backlog.spec: Add a generator that builds 26 starting centers from a small parameter vector: a number of rows (5 or 6), a per-row count (summing to 26, drawn from a fixed list of compositions such as [5,5,5,5,6], [4,5,4,5,4,4]), a horizontal stagger offset per row, and a vertical squeeze factor. Enumerate every composition in the list with a fixed seed, build each layout, run _relax briefly, then _slsqp_refine on the best 3 by LP score. Use the resulting best as an additional member in the coarse population of _two_phase. This is an architecture change to the initial layout family, not a new search loop.
backlog.title: Parametric row-template generator refined by SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random seeds in the coarse phase of _two_phase with Bridson-style Poisson-disk samples in [0.05, 0.95]^2. For each seed draw a minimum spacing d_min uniformly from [0.12, 0.22] and rejection-sample up to 26 points with a fixed-seed RandomState; if fewer than 26 points are accepted, fill the rest uniformly. Pass these starts through the existing _relax call unchanged. This changes only the initial point distribution, so the population still uses the same selection and recombination logic.
backlog.title: Poisson-disk seeded starts with variable minimum spacing

backlog.spec: In the coarse phase of _two_phase, before calling _relax, draw a weight vector w with entries uniform in [0.6, 1.4] (fixed-seed RandomState per start) and replace the per-radius growth step in _relax with growth scaled by w_i, so larger-weight circles inflate faster. Score the final configuration with the unweighted LP as usual (_score), so selection still uses the true sum of radii. This regularises the early dynamics toward a broader set of size distributions without touching the scoring.
backlog.title: Random positive-weight objective to diversify basins

backlog.spec: Add a Monte Carlo compression stage that treats the box side L as a variable. Start from the current best centers rescaled to a box of side 1.0. Repeat for a fixed number of sweeps: propose random single-circle displacements of size 0.02 and box-scale moves of L by a factor in [0.999, 1.001], accepting a move only if no pair overlaps at radius 0.5 times the current minimum inter-center distance minus the wall constraints (use a fixed-seed RandomState). Use a pressure parameter P that is increased geometrically across sweeps so the box shrinks. Finish by mapping back to the unit square, then run _score and _slsqp_refine on the result. Keep this as a standalone candidate generator that competes in the existing best-of comparison.
backlog.title: Hard-disk NPT Monte Carlo compression with a variable box

backlog.spec: Alternate between two subproblems. (a) Fix the current radii r and maximise t subject to ||c_i - c_j|| >= t*(r_i + r_j) for all pairs and walls (r_i <= x_i, y_i, 1-x_i, 1-y_i scaled by t), using SLSQP on the variables (centers, t) with analytic constraint Jacobians if possible. (b) Fix the centers and solve the existing _lp_radii LP. Repeat 5 to 8 times with a fixed seed, starting from the incumbent. Accept an iterate only if the LP sum improves. This gives a different descent direction from the joint SLSQP already in place, and it is a fully deterministic polish.
backlog.title: Epigraph max-min slack alternation with LP radii

backlog.spec: Define a small parameter vector for the generator: stagger offset, vertical squeeze, boundary-margin, and relax learning rate. Evaluate 6 initial parameter sets in one batch (each run through _relax then _score with a fixed seed), then for 12 more rounds fit a simple quadratic-regression surrogate on all evaluated points and propose 4 candidates by minimising the surrogate inside the box with a fixed-seed random search; evaluate those 4 as a batch. Keep the best packing across all evaluations and pass it to the existing _slsqp_refine. The batch of 4 evaluations per round is the unit of work, so the design favours parallel-friendly rounds.
backlog.title: Batch Bayesian-style surrogate over layout parameters

backlog.spec: Split the square into a left half and a right half (vertical cut at x=0.5 with a small free gap). Assign 13 circles to each side by a fixed-seed random partition, and pack each half independently in its own rectangle [0,0.5]x[0,1] or [0.5,1]x[0,1] using a short _relax plus _slsqp_refine with the wall bounds rescaled to that rectangle. Then recombine the 26 centers, run _relax with the full square walls at low learning rate to remove the seam, and polish with _slsqp_refine. Try the cut in both orientations and keep the best by LP score. This is a hierarchical construction, separate from the mirror-symmetric start already tried.
backlog.title: Two-half divide and conquer with merge refinement

backlog.spec: Maintain an archive of all packings evaluated in the coarse phase. For each packing compute a behaviour descriptor: the sorted histogram of contact counts (pairs with gap below 1e-3) plus a quantised radius-sum profile into 4 bins. Replace the worst-score population member rule in _two_phase with a novelty score: for each candidate, average distance to its 5 nearest archive descriptors, and accept a child into the population if its novelty exceeds the population median or its LP score is in the top half. Keep a fixed seed and the same time budget. This shifts selection from pure score toward distinct contact structures.
backlog.title: Novelty-driven archive selection for the coarse population

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 80-iteration SLSQP budget and constant perturbation in the basin-hopping loop of construct_packing with restarts scheduled by the Luby sequence (1,1,2,1,1,2,4,...). Each restart length in iterations sets how many basin-hopping steps are taken from the current best before a reset to the best-so-far with a fresh random perturbation of the 3 most loosely constrained centers (lowest LP dual). Track the Luby index with a counter, use a fixed seed, and keep the existing _relax and _score calls. This changes only the outer scheduling of the existing search.
backlog.title: Luby-sequence restart budgets for basin hopping

backlog.spec: After the incumbent is scored, build the Delaunay triangulation of the centres (scipy.spatial.Delaunay). Pick a random interior edge whose two opposite triangle vertices are not already in contact, and flip it so the edge connects the two opposite vertices. Then relax with _relax (200 steps, lr_c 0.05, lr_r 0.01, lam 0.5 toward the pre-flip centres), run _slsqp_refine with maxiter 80, and accept with the existing score-based acceptance rule. Use a fixed seed. Each basin-hopping iteration does one flip with probability 0.3 and a Gaussian move otherwise. This changes the topology of the contact graph, which the current moves never do.
backlog.title: Delaunay edge-flip moves on the contact graph

backlog.spec: Enumerate candidate sets of circles that touch each wall. For each candidate, fix those circles to be tangent to the corresponding wall by setting their coordinate to r_i, then solve the max-radii problem as a linear program in the remaining variables with those equalities. Keep the best few sets. Choose the candidate sets by sampling a fixed number of random wall-touch patterns (for example 60 patterns with 6 to 10 wall-touching circles), using a fixed seed. Feed the best pattern's centres into _relax and _slsqp_refine as the seed for the basin-hopping stage. The point is to make the boundary structure explicit rather than leaving it to the penalty dynamics.
backlog.title: Wall-contact enumeration with constrained LP

backlog.spec: Build packings by beam search instead of a single greedy chain. Start from an empty list of centres. At each step, propose insertion candidates on a 40 by 40 grid (plus small jitter), keep the top 8 by largest free hole (min of distance to the nearest centre and twice the wall distance), and for each partial configuration compute a cheap proxy score: the sum of radii from a greedy radius assignment. Keep the top 6 partial packings at each depth. At depth 26, run the exact _lp_radii score on each survivor, then pass the best 5 through _relax and _slsqp_refine. Fixed seed, and stop early if the total wall time exceeds 120 seconds.
backlog.title: Beam search over greedy insertion sequences

backlog.spec: Discretise the square into a 60 by 60 grid of candidate centre positions. Represent a configuration as 26 distinct grid indices. Run simulated annealing where a move relocates one circle to a random empty grid cell, or swaps the positions of two circles of different radius. Score every candidate by the exact _lp_radii sum on the continuous centres. Temperature decays geometrically from 0.01 to 0.0001 over the time budget. Once the discrete search stops improving, lift the best discrete configuration back to continuous coordinates and run _relax and _slsqp_refine to remove the grid bias. Use a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Fine-grid discrete simulated annealing on occupancy

backlog.spec: Build a starting configuration by agglomerative pairing. Take 13 random seeds and place each one as a dimer: two circles of unequal radius, one large and one small, at a fixed offset along a random direction. Scale the dimer centres so they fill the square, then run _relax with the dimers as the initial state so the large members of each dimer move apart. Afterwards, break the dimer constraint by letting all 26 centres move freely under _relax with lam 0.2 toward the dimer layout, then finish with _slsqp_refine. Use a fixed seed and make this one of the population members in the coarse phase, replacing one random member per run.
backlog.title: Agglomerative dimer start with later splitting

backlog.spec: Speed up the exact scoring so the basin-hopping stage performs more iterations in the same time budget. In _lp_radii, keep only pairs whose centre distance is below a cutoff of 2.6 times the current maximum radius estimate (the neighbour list), which typically removes over 80 percent of the 325 pair constraints. Solve the reduced LP with linprog(method='highs'). Then compute all pair slacks with the solution and add any violated pair back into the constraint set. Repeat until no violation remains, so the result is still exact. Use the time saved to raise the basin-hopping iteration budget and keep the wall-time guard at 215 seconds.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour-list LP with reinvested time

backlog.spec: Generate starting layouts from a spectral embedding. Draw a random geometric graph on 26 vertices with a fixed seed, joining pairs whose distance is below a random threshold. Compute the two lowest nontrivial eigenvectors of its normalised graph Laplacian and use them as x and y coordinates, then rescale both coordinates into [0.08, 0.92]. Repeat for 40 seeds and keep the 12 layouts with the largest spread (minimum pairwise distance). Feed them to the existing _relax and _slsqp_refine pipeline as population members in place of uniform random draws, keeping the rest of _two_phase unchanged.
backlog.title: Graph-Laplacian spectral starting layouts

backlog.spec: Structure the coarse search by the number k of circles that touch the boundary. For k in 14, 16, 18, 20, generate starting configurations where exactly k circles are placed on the boundary of the square at evenly spaced positions with a fixed seed, and the rest are placed uniformly in the interior. Run _relax with lr_c 0.2 and then _slsqp_refine on each, and record the LP score. Pick the best k and then run the existing _two_phase population search seeded from the top three configurations across all k. This gives the search an explicit boundary-count dimension, which the current search never varies.
backlog.title: Beam over the number of wall-touching circles

backlog.spec: Replace the joint relaxation with an alternating scheme in which radii are frozen at the incumbent values. Move centres to maximise the minimum slack, defined as the smallest of (pair distance minus radius sum) and (wall distance minus radius). Solve this with a short sequence of linear programs in the displacement variables, using the slack constraints linearised at the current centres and a box trust region of 0.02. After each centre update, call _lp_radii to refresh the radii. Iterate until the sum of radii stops increasing by more than 1e-7 or 50 rounds are reached. Use it as a final polish after _slsqp_refine.
backlog.title: Frozen-radius alternation with max-min slack

backlog.spec: Optimise a smoothed surrogate of the sum of radii before switching to the exact objective. Replace the linear objective in _slsqp_refine with the power-mean sum of r_i raised to p, where p starts at 0.5 and rises to 1.0 across three stages with a fixed seed. Within each stage, call _slsqp_refine with maxiter 60 on the same pair and wall constraints. Concave p below 1 spreads the radii more evenly and can move the search out of basins where a few large circles dominate. The final stage uses p equal to 1 and is followed by _lp_radii and _make_valid as before. Keep the population and basin hopping stages unchanged.
backlog.title: Power-mean objective continuation

backlog.spec: Replace the penalty-only refinement with an augmented Lagrangian method over z = [centers, radii]. Maximise sum(r) subject to the pair constraints d_ij - r_i - r_j >= 0 and the four wall constraints. For each constraint keep a multiplier lambda >= 0, initialised to zero. Minimise L(z) = -sum(r) + sum over constraints of (mu/2)*(max(0, lambda/mu - g))^2 with L-BFGS-B, using analytic gradients and the existing bounds. After each inner solve, update lambda = max(0, lambda - mu*g) and increase mu by 2x while the maximum violation is above 1e-9. Run about 6 outer iterations from the best basin-hopping packing, then pass the centers to _lp_radii and _make_valid so the returned packing is exactly valid.
backlog.title: Augmented Lagrangian on joint centers and radii

backlog.spec: Replace the Metropolis acceptance in the construct_packing loop with late-acceptance hill climbing. Keep a circular history buffer of length 50 holding past accepted LP scores, initialised to the starting score. A candidate with score s is accepted if s >= history[k] or s >= current score, where k = iteration mod 50. After each step, write the current score into history[k]. This removes the temperature parameter T entirely. Keep the same perturbation moves, _relax and _slsqp_refine calls, and the best-so-far tracking. Use a fixed seed so runs are repeatable.
backlog.title: Late-acceptance hill climbing in the outer loop

backlog.spec: Smooth the LP score before accepting moves. For each candidate center set c, draw K=6 fixed-seed Gaussian jitters with standard deviation 1e-3 applied to the centers, clip to [0,1], evaluate _score on each, and use the mean of the valid sums as the candidate's acceptance value. Keep the exact unsmoothed best for the returned answer, scored only on the un-jittered centers via _score and _make_valid. This makes the acceptance landscape flatter near narrow ridges where the LP is sharply nonsmooth. Use it only in the basin-hopping acceptance test and leave the other stages unchanged.
backlog.title: Randomized-smoothing score for acceptance

backlog.spec: Add a new start generator to the coarse phase. Lay out a 5x5 square grid of centers at coordinates (i+0.5)/5 for i in 0..4, giving 25 points. Add one extra center at a fixed-seed random location in [0.2,0.8]^2. Shift the grid with a small fixed-seed jitter of scale 0.01 and clip to [0.05,0.95]. Use this start for roughly one fifth of the coarse-phase population slots, relax it with _relax using the same parameters as the random starts, then score it with _score. The rest of the population and the crossover stage stay unchanged. The aim is a deliberately different basin family from the hexagonal and ring starts already tried.
backlog.title: Square-grid start with one defect

backlog.spec: Add a new perturbation move to the basin-hopping loop that acts on radii rather than centers. Take the current best radii and multiply them by a factor drawn uniformly from [1.02, 1.08]. Run _relax with the centers unchanged for 150 steps and a small center learning rate of 0.01 so that overlaps push the centers apart, then rescore with _score. This is a single kick that opens space in the current basin without the random center jumps used by the other moves. Accept it using the existing LP score test. Use a fixed seed and keep the move probability at 0.2, with the other moves taking the remaining probability.
backlog.title: Radius-space inflation kick with LP-scored acceptance

backlog.spec: Add a stage that optimises circle centers in polar coordinates about the square center (0.5, 0.5). Each center is written as (0.5 + rho*cos(theta), 0.5 + rho*sin(theta)) with rho and theta as the optimisation variables, and rho is clipped to [0, 0.7]. Starting from the best packing, convert the centers to (rho, theta), run the existing joint SLSQP over the radii and the polar variables with the wall and pair constraints re-expressed through the chain rule, or with finite differences if that is simpler, and then convert back. Keep the result only if _score improves. This changes the geometry of the search space, since moves toward or away from the center become one-dimensional. It is a fallback stage, so it runs only after basin hopping.
backlog.title: Polar-coordinate reparametrisation of centers

backlog.spec: Change the random start distribution in the coarse population to a boundary-biased one. For each coordinate draw u from a Beta(0.6, 0.6) distribution using the fixed-seed rng, then map it to [0.05, 0.95]. This puts more mass near the walls than the current uniform [0.1, 0.9] draws, which tends to create wall-touching circles that the optimum needs. Keep the same _relax call and _score as before. Use Beta draws for half of the coarse population and uniform draws for the other half, so both kinds of start stay in the pool. Keep the crossover and the rest of the search unchanged.
backlog.title: Edge-biased Beta-distributed random starts

backlog.spec: Add a new start generator for the coarse phase of _two_phase. Map 26 points to a Hilbert space-filling curve over [0,1]^2 (order 3 gives 64 cells; take 26 evenly spaced cells along the curve, then jitter by a fixed-seed N(0, 0.01)). Use these centers as one population member, then run the existing _relax and _score path unchanged. Include it as a candidate alongside the existing random members, so selection keeps it only if the LP score wins. Use only numpy, with the Hilbert index computed by the standard iterative bit-rotation routine.
backlog.title: Hilbert-curve ordered start with greedy radii

backlog.spec: Before the coarse phase, find the largest common radius r* for which 26 equal circles fit in the unit square, by bisection on r with a feasibility test. The test is a penalty relaxation: centers start random under a fixed seed, and gradient steps on the sum of squared overlap and wall violations run for about 300 iterations, with success if the total violation falls below 1e-8. Use the resulting feasible centers, scaled down to a radius of 0.97 r*, as a second population seed. Its LP-maximised radii then give a non-uniform start that often sits near a good basin. Keep the bisection to about 12 steps so the cost stays inside the time budget.
backlog.title: Equal-radius feasibility bisection start

backlog.spec: Inside the SLSQP refinement, replace the uniform pair constraints with weighted ones. Keep a weight w_ij for each pair, initialised to 1. Run a short SLSQP, then update w_ij by multiplying with exp(eta * active_slack) for pairs whose gap is below 1e-4 at the solution, and renormalise to mean 1. Repeat for 4 rounds, and keep the best LP-scored result across rounds. The weights act as Lagrange-like multipliers that shift effort toward the pairs that actually bind, which may escape the plateau seen in basin hopping. Use only numpy and scipy, and keep the total wall time under the existing budget.
backlog.title: Multiplicative-weights pair-constraint emphasis

backlog.spec: Add a Langevin-style sampler over center vectors as a new stage after _two_phase. At each step, compute the score S(c) = sum of LP radii (scored by _score). Propose c' = c + eta * grad + sqrt(2 * eta * T) * noise, where the gradient is estimated by central finite differences on a random subset of 6 circles (each with step 1e-4), and the noise is drawn from a fixed-seed RandomState. Accept with a Metropolis rule on S. Lower T geometrically from 2e-3 to 1e-5 over the run. Track the best valid packing. This differs from the existing annealing and basin hopping because the move is driven by a gradient estimate, not by a blind Gaussian kick.
backlog.title: Langevin dynamics on the LP-scored packing

backlog.spec: Add a search that restricts moves to a random low-dimensional subspace of the 52-dimensional center space. Draw a fixed-seed random matrix P of shape (52, 6) with orthonormal columns from QR. Starting from the incumbent centers, optimise the 6 coefficients z with a Nelder-Mead or coordinate pattern search, where each evaluation sets c = c0 + P z, clips to [0,1], runs a short _relax with the incumbent as template, and scores with _score. Repeat with fresh subspaces for a fixed number of rounds. Accept any round that improves the LP score, and then return to the full-dimensional basin hopping. The reduced space gives large, structured moves that the isotropic Gaussian kicks cannot produce.
backlog.title: Random low-dimensional subspace search

backlog.spec: Add a zeroth-order (evolution-strategies) optimiser over the 52 center coordinates, scored by the exact LP sum of radii. Each generation draws 8 antithetic Gaussian perturbations with sigma 0.003 from a fixed-seed RandomState, evaluates each with _score (skipping infeasible ones), and forms a gradient estimate as the weighted sum of perturbations, using rank-based weights. Take a step of size 0.002 along that estimate, and anneal sigma by 0.97 per generation when no improvement occurs. Run for as long as the time budget allows, and return the best valid packing. This is a different gradient signal from the existing finite-difference and LP-dual moves, because it uses the LP value directly.
backlog.title: Zeroth-order gradient ascent on the LP score

backlog.spec: Add a regularisation term that targets rattlers, meaning circles whose LP radius is far below the typical radius and which sit in loose cages. After each basin-hopping stage, compute the radii from _score. Pick the circle with the smallest radius, and, for a fixed-seed random subset of 4 candidate slots from the largest empty holes on a 60 by 60 grid, relocate it to the slot that maximises the distance to its nearest neighbour. Then rerun _relax and _slsqp_refine with the pair constraints. Accept the move only if the LP score improves. This is distinct from the earlier reinsertion move because it is triggered only on rattlers identified from the LP solution, and the candidate slots are restricted to the grid holes.
backlog.title: Soft rattler-escape penalty on small radii

backlog.spec: Add a population seed built from a smaller problem. First run the existing coarse-and-refine search for 25 circles (fixed seed, about 60 seconds). Then insert the 26th circle at the grid point (on a 80 by 80 grid) with the largest distance to its nearest center and largest wall clearance. Run _relax on the 26-circle set with the 25-circle centers as template, then _slsqp_refine and _score. Put the resulting packing into the 12-member population before the crossover stage. This gives a structured start that is different from random seeds, and it reuses the code paths already in train.py.
backlog.title: Two-stage n=25 seed with insertion of the 26th circle

backlog.spec: Add a batch of short restarts in which each start is forced to have a fixed number of circles touching the walls. Pick a quota q from {12, 14, 16, 18, 20} for each restart (cycled deterministically). Before _relax, pin the q circles nearest the boundary to lie on it by projecting their centers to the nearest wall (fixed seed for the choice). Run _relax with the pinned circles fixed in position as a soft constraint (apply a quadratic pull weight 0.5 toward the projection), then run _slsqp_refine unconstrained and _score. Keep the best packing across restarts. This explores the boundary-contact structure directly, which the random-seed population does not do.
backlog.title: Multi-restart with deliberate wall-count quotas

backlog.spec: Add a curriculum on the radius bound used in the joint SLSQP. Start with the radius upper bound set to 0.10 for every circle, which forces the search to fill space with many small circles. Run _slsqp_refine on the centers and radii with this cap. Then raise the cap in three steps to 0.20, 0.30, and 0.50 (the original bound), rerunning _slsqp_refine at each step from the previous solution. Score with _score and keep the best valid packing. This is a continuation in the bound parameter rather than in the penalty or temperature, and it may steer the solution away from the basin the unconstrained radius growth falls into.
backlog.title: Radius-cap curriculum on the joint problem

backlog.spec: Add a new optimizer _slp_refine(c, r, iters=30) that linearises the pair distances d_ij = ||c_i - c_j|| and the wall terms around the current (c, r) and solves, with scipy linprog (HiGHS), for a step (dc, dr) that maximises sum(r + dr) subject to linearised pair constraints d_ij + g_ij.(dc_i - dc_j) >= r_i + dr_i + r_j + dr_j, linearised wall constraints, and a box trust region |dc|, |dr| <= delta. Accept the step if the exact score (_score on the new centres) improves, and then grow delta by 1.5x; otherwise shrink delta by 0.5x. Stop when delta < 1e-7 or after iters. Call it on the output of _two_phase and on the basin-hopping candidates in place of or after _slsqp_refine. Keep everything fixed-seed. This is a different local optimiser from SLSQP and should converge to tighter contact sets.
backlog.title: Sequential linear programming with trust region on joint centres and radii

backlog.spec: Add a construction that builds a packing one circle at a time by tangency rather than by relaxation. Start with the largest circle tangent to two walls in a corner. For each new circle, enumerate candidate positions that are tangent to two already-placed objects (circles or walls) and take the candidate with the largest feasible radius, where the radius is min over all existing objects of the distance minus their radius, capped at 0.25. Use a fixed-seed random choice among the top three candidates for diversity over 200 random construction orders. Each completed construction is passed to _score (exact LP) and the best is kept as a population member for _two_phase. It is a new architecture: incremental tangency placement, not the grid insertion or relaxation already in the file.
backlog.title: Apollonian tangency-chain constructive packing

backlog.spec: Add a discrete stage that uses scipy.optimize.milp (HiGHS) to choose which of K = 7x7 grid cell centres each of the 26 circles occupies. Binary variables x_{i,k} with sum_k x_{i,k} = 1 and sum_i x_{i,k} <= 1, objective maximise sum_{i,k} x_{i,k} * w_k, where w_k is a cell score equal to the distance of the cell centre from the nearest wall, plus a spread term that penalises pairs of cells closer than 0.14 through conflict constraints x_{i,k} + x_{j,l} <= 1 for close pairs. Convert the chosen cells to continuous centres with a fixed-seed jitter of 0.02, then run _relax and _score. Use the best of several MILP solutions obtained under different fixed-seed conflict thresholds as an extra population seed for _two_phase. The MILP is time-limited to 20 seconds. This is a genuinely combinatorial, exact-solver approach.
backlog.title: MILP cell assignment of circles to a coarse grid, then exact LP radii

backlog.spec: Add a data-parametrised start with few parameters. Generate a triangular lattice with 26 points scaled into [0.1, 0.9]^2 using a fixed-seed random rotation and row offset. Add a smooth displacement field dc_i = sum over modes (m, n) with m, n in {0, 1, 2} of a_{mn} cos(m pi x_i) cos(n pi y_i) for each coordinate, where the 2x2x... coefficients a are drawn from a fixed-seed normal with scale 0.05. Sample 40 such parameter sets, run _relax on each with short steps, score them with _score, and keep the best 4 as population seeds for _two_phase. This searches a 18-dimensional smooth subspace of layouts instead of 52 free coordinates, which is a different parametrisation from the random subspace and the template ideas already tried.
backlog.title: Low-order cosine deformation of a triangular lattice

backlog.spec: Add a new relaxation _relax_nesterov(c, r, steps, lr, beta=0.9) as an alternative to _relax. Define the energy E = sum over pairs of max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)^2 + sum over walls of max(0, r_i - wall distance)^2 with radii held fixed at the current values. Run Nesterov accelerated gradient descent on the centre coordinates with momentum beta, a learning rate that halves whenever the energy rises, and a stop when E < 1e-12. Within each outer step, grow the radii by a fixed amount where the energy is zero. Use this relaxation in place of _relax for the population seeds in _two_phase and for the basin-hopping candidates. This is a second-order-like physical dynamics with inertia, unlike the current first-order repulsion steps.
backlog.title: Nesterov momentum relaxation on the overlap energy

backlog.spec: Replace every time.time() guard in _two_phase and construct_packing with a fixed iteration count chosen so that the expected run stays under 200 seconds on one CPU thread. Measure nothing at runtime. Set the coarse phase to 40 random starts, the crossover phase to 150 children, the refinement to the top 5, and the basin-hopping loop to 600 iterations, with the iteration counts scaled by a constant calibrated so that the whole run is about 3 to 4 minutes. Keep the fixed seeds. The result becomes exactly repeatable across machines, which removes the 1e-6 noise and makes replicate runs comparable. This is a schedule change only; it should not change the search structure.
backlog.title: Deterministic iteration budget instead of wall-clock cut-offs

backlog.spec: Add a two-stage radii solve for fixed centres. Stage one solves the epigraph LP that maximises t subject to r_i >= t for all i with pair and wall constraints, then fixes t' = 0.995 t as a lower bound on every radius. Stage two solves the usual sum-of-radii LP under these lower bounds. Use the two-stage result as the score in _score and as the final radii in _make_valid. Apply this only in the final 30 seconds of construct_packing, on the best 3 candidates, and keep the single-stage result if the two-stage sum is lower. The lower-bound floor discourages degenerate solutions where a few circles shrink to zero and yields a more balanced radius profile before the sum is maximised.
backlog.title: Lexicographic max-min-then-sum LP with contact-set pinning

backlog.spec: Add a large-neighbourhood move to the basin-hopping loop in construct_packing. Pick a fixed-seed random window centre p and remove the k = 5 to 7 circles nearest to p. Reinsert them one at a time, each at the grid point (on a 41x41 grid) with the largest free hole value min(distance to other circles, twice the wall distance), with a fixed-seed jitter of 0.004. Then run _relax with 150 steps, _slsqp_refine with 60 iterations, and _score. Accept by the same Metropolis rule as the current loop. This differs from the single-circle grid reinsertion and from the random subset relaxation because it removes a spatial cluster and rebuilds it in one batch.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood destroy-and-repair on spatial windows

backlog.spec: Add a two-tier radius start. Choose a fixed number of large radius targets (6 circles at 0.17) and small targets (20 circles at 0.09). Build a candidate slot set from 26 points of a 5x6 staggered grid with fixed-seed jitter. Solve a linear assignment (scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment) between the 26 slots and the 26 target radii using the cost matrix of distances from each slot to the nearest wall minus the target radius, so that large radii go to roomy slots. Set centres to the assigned slots and radii to the targets, run _relax with the radii fixed for 200 steps, then _score. Produce 30 such starts with different fixed-seed jitters, keep the best 4 as population seeds for _two_phase. This is a different assignment-based seed from the earlier prescribed-profile and mixed-size starts.
backlog.title: Hungarian assignment of radius classes to lattice-like slots

backlog.spec: After _two_phase, treat f(centers) = LP optimum of sum of radii as a nonsmooth concave-type function of the 52 center coordinates. Use a proximal bundle method: at each step, collect the last K (about 20) (centers, value, subgradient) triples, where the subgradient for each center comes from the LP dual multipliers on active pair and wall constraints (d/dc of d_ij = unit vector). Solve a small QP (scipy minimize SLSQP on the bundle model with a trust radius of 0.01 that adapts by the ratio of actual to predicted gain). Accept a step only if the exact LP score improves. Stop at a fixed iteration count of about 150 or the time budget.
backlog.title: Bundle method on the nonsmooth LP value

backlog.spec: Replace the hard-max overlap in a fixed-radius stage with an analytic-gradient Adam optimizer (lr 0.002, beta1 0.9, beta2 0.999). Radii are set to the current LP radii scaled by 1.02 for the target. The energy is the sum over pairs and walls of softplus(-gap/tau) squared, with tau annealed geometrically from 0.05 to 0.0005 over 1500 steps. Use the gradient of the energy w.r.t. centers only. After each 100 steps, compute the exact LP score and keep the best centers. Feed the best result to the existing SLSQP refine. The fixed seed controls only the initial jitter.
backlog.title: Adam on log-sum-exp overlap energy with annealed temperature

backlog.spec: Keep the five best packings from _two_phase as an elite set. For each ordered pair (A, B) of elite members, match circles between A and B by a minimum-cost assignment (scipy linear_sum_assignment on the distance matrix). Walk from A toward B in 10 equal interpolation steps of the matched centers, and at each interior point run the existing _relax with a small step, then score with the exact LP. Keep the best interior point found on any path as a new candidate, and pass it through _slsqp_refine. Use a fixed seed for any tie-breaking. Stop when the time budget is spent.
backlog.title: Path relinking between elite packings

backlog.spec: Optimize the packing inside a rectangle of width a and height 1 for a in a schedule of values such as 0.95, 0.975, 1.0, 1.025, 1.05, using the existing relax and SLSQP stages with wall constraints at 0 and a. After each solve, apply the affine map x to x/a, y to y, so that the packing lands in the unit square. Recompute the exact LP radii in the unit square, because the affine map changes pair distances. Keep the candidate with the largest valid sum, and then run the existing basin hopping from it. This explores container shapes that are close to the square.
backlog.title: Anisotropic container continuation

backlog.spec: Build a coarse problem of 20 super-circles by greedily merging the closest pair of circles 6 times, with each super-circle placed at the weighted centroid and carrying a mass equal to the number of merged circles. Solve the coarse packing by the existing _relax and _slsqp_refine stages, where a super-circle's radius is set to the sum of its members' areas, scaled to fit. Uncoarsen by splitting each super-circle into its member circles, placed at offsets along the local principal direction of the cluster with a fixed-seed jitter of 0.01. Then run _relax on the full 26-circle set and finish with the exact LP and SLSQP. Use this output as a population seed for the coarse phase.
backlog.title: Multilevel coarsening and uncoarsening

backlog.spec: Ignore the radii for the first stage. Maximize the minimum over pairs and walls of the ratio gap_ij / (r_i + r_j), where the radii are fixed to a target profile of 26 values with the same pattern as the incumbent LP solution. Use a smooth min via softmin with a sharpness annealed from 10 to 300, and optimize the centers with the analytic gradient in scipy L-BFGS-B. Each time the ratio is improved, rescale the target radii by the new minimum ratio. Finish with the existing exact LP and SLSQP. This is a different objective from the sum of radii that can escape the current basin.
backlog.title: Scale-invariant max-min ratio optimization

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed time cut-offs in construct_packing with a controller. Keep a running record of the LP score gain per second for three move types: grid-hole reinsertion, local Gaussian kick, and the new dislocation move. Every 20 iterations, allocate the next 20 iterations to the move type with the best gain per second, with a 10 percent exploration floor. Use the same fixed seed. The controller replaces only the move-choice logic and changes no physics.
backlog.title: Elite-fraction time allocation controller

backlog.spec: Model each circle as a node in a spring network with rest length r_i + r_j for each neighbouring pair (those within 1.3 times the sum of radii), and wall springs with rest length r_i. Use the LP radii as the target. Relax the centers by gradient descent on the spring energy, with the spring stiffness ramped from 0.1 to 10 over 400 steps. This pulls near-contact pairs to exact contact while keeping the topology fixed. Then score with the exact LP and run the existing SLSQP refine. Use this as a polish stage after _two_phase.
backlog.title: Spring network with stiffness annealing toward LP radii

backlog.spec: Split the square into four quadrants. Assign circles to quadrants by a fixed-seed draw with counts 7, 6, 6, 7. Solve each quadrant as an independent packing in a unit sub-square, using the existing _two_phase style with fewer iterations. Map the solutions into the full square with the matching scale of 0.5, then run _relax on the full 26-circle set to remove boundary overlaps, followed by the exact LP and SLSQP refine. Keep the best result over three seeds for the quadrant split.
backlog.title: Quadrant-split with boundary-matched merge

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, pick a random disc of radius 0.2 in the square and remove all circles whose centers lie inside it, up to a maximum of 6. Reinsert them one at a time at the grid points with the largest distance to the remaining centers, using a 30 by 30 grid and a wall-distance cap. Then run _relax for 100 steps, the exact LP score, and accept by the same Metropolis rule. This differs from the existing large-neighbourhood move by using a spatial disc instead of a spatial window, and by allowing reinsertion anywhere in the square.
backlog.title: Iterated greedy destruction with exact LP acceptance

backlog.spec: Add a search stage that imposes both mirror symmetries x -> 1-x and y -> 1-y. Use free parameters for generic quadrant orbits (4 circles each, mirrored to (x,y),(1-x,y),(x,1-y),(1-x,1-y)) plus on-axis pairs on x=0.5 or y=0.5 (orbit size 2) to reach 26, e.g. 6 generic orbits plus 1 axis pair. Optimise these few parameters with the existing LP scorer under a fixed seed and a small Nelder-Mead or coordinate search, then unfold to the full 26 centres and run the existing joint SLSQP and basin hopping on the unsymmetrised configuration. Keep the best of the symmetric and unsymmetric results.
backlog.title: Dihedral D2 symmetric search (both mirror axes)

backlog.spec: Replace the constant temperature T=0.002 in the basin-hopping loop with a cyclic schedule: T decays geometrically from 0.01 to 0.0002 over each cycle of about 60 iterations, then jumps back up to restart the cycle from the best-so-far centres. Keep the existing grid-hole reinsertion and SLSQP refinement. Use a fixed seed and the same wall-clock guard, and log the cycle index only for debugging.
backlog.title: Cyclic reheating schedule for basin hopping

backlog.spec: Partition the 26 circles into 4 to 6 clusters with fixed-seed k-means on random seeds. Pack each cluster in a sub-box of the unit square using a small local relax plus SLSQP run with the box treated as its own container. Place cluster boxes on a coarse grid (for example 2x3 or 3x3 slots with varying widths chosen from a fixed list), then run the global relax, LP radii and joint SLSQP on the assembled 26-centre layout. Accept the assembled layout only if its LP score beats the current population best.
backlog.title: Hierarchical cluster-then-assemble construction

backlog.spec: Before the square-container search, solve the same problem in a superellipse container |2x-1|^p + |2y-1|^p <= 1 starting from p=2 (disk) and continue p toward a large value that approximates the square (p = 2, 4, 8, 16, 32). At each p, relax the centres with the existing _relax using the container-distance function replaced by the superellipse signed distance, then use the LP for radii under the square constraints. Feed the p=32 result as an extra population member to the existing coarse-plus-refine phase.
backlog.title: Superellipse container homotopy

backlog.spec: After the LP scoring, compute the contact graph (pairs with gap below 1e-7 and walls touched) and the rank of its Jacobian. Circles whose column is not needed to keep the rank (rattlers) are removed and the remaining 25 or fewer circles are re-scored by LP.
