Reinsert each rattler at the largest grid hole of the reduced packing, then run the joint SLSQP once. Keep whichever packing has the larger exact LP sum.
backlog.title: Subset rigidity check to target rattlers

backlog.spec: Replace the per-candidate LP with a two-stage bound: first compute a cheap upper bound on the sum of radii by an LP on the pair constraints with the nearest 8 neighbours of each circle only, then run the full LP only for candidates whose bound exceeds 0.98 times the current best. This keeps the search exact on accepted states while letting the basin-hopping loop evaluate many more moves per second. Use a fixed seed so results are reproducible.
backlog.title: Exact radii via interval-bounded LP envelope

backlog.spec: Add a final polish stage that solves a sequence of LPs with objective sum_i w_i r_i, where the weights come from the dual multipliers of the previous LP plus a small epsilon, so that circles whose constraints are slack get smaller weights. Iterate 5 to 8 times with fixed weights recomputed each step. Accept the final radii only after _make_valid and an exact LP check of the same centres.
backlog.title: Weighted-sum lexicographic radius-profile objective

backlog.spec: Stack 16 perturbed copies of the current best centre set into a (16, 26, 2) array, run the existing _relax update as a single numpy broadcast over the batch axis for 150 steps, then score each copy with the LP and keep the best. Repeat this batch step inside the basin-hopping loop in place of one-at-a-time moves, with a fixed seed. The batch dimension avoids Python loops and is the only change to the move generator.
backlog.title: Batch of centre perturbations evaluated as one vectorised relax

backlog.spec: Seed the coarse phase with an alternative population member: radii drawn from a fixed geometric ladder (ratio 0.85 between successive sizes, largest 0.2) assigned to random centres, then relaxed with the existing _relax and LP scored. Use this only for one population slot out of 12 so the existing random and crossover starts remain dominant. Keep the seed fixed and record which slot produced the final best.
backlog.title: Mixed-size start from a fixed radius ladder

backlog.spec: Add a per-call maximum displacement bound to the joint SLSQP variables: each centre coordinate is restricted to [c0 - delta, c0 + delta] where c0 is the starting centre and delta decays from 0.05 to 0.002 over successive calls in the basin-hopping loop. This replaces the single broad bounds in _slsqp_refine for the loop only and tests whether smaller joint moves polish the basin better. Keep the exact LP score as the accept test.
backlog.title: Time-decaying trust region on the joint SLSQP

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop of construct_packing, replace the Gaussian centre perturbation with heavy-tailed Levy steps. Draw each step as Mantegna's algorithm with exponent alpha=1.5 (u ~ N(0, sigma_u^2), v ~ N(0,1), step = u/|v|^(1/alpha)), scale by 0.02, and apply it to one randomly chosen circle (occasionally two). Keep the existing relax, SLSQP and LP scoring, and the same fixed seed. Occasional long jumps should escape basins that small Gaussian moves cannot leave.
backlog.title: Levy-flight basin hopping

backlog.spec: Replace the box bounds on centres in _slsqp_refine with an unconstrained parametrisation: centre = 0.5*(1+tanh(z)) (or a sigmoid), and radii = softplus(w). Run an unconstrained L-BFGS on a smooth penalty of the pair and wall violations (squared hinge), with the penalty weight increasing across 4 stages, then hand the result to the existing SLSQP with ordinary constraints. The aim is to remove active-bound degeneracy at the walls, which the current bounds create.
backlog.title: Sigmoid box reparametrisation for the joint problem

backlog.spec: Maintain a dictionary of visited local optima keyed by a signature: the sorted radii rounded to 3 decimals together with the number of wall contacts and the number of pair contacts within 1e-6. In the basin-hopping loop, when a refined candidate hits a known signature, do not re-score or accept it as new and instead count it as a failed move. After 40 consecutive duplicate hits, force a random restart from the population pool. This reallocates the time budget to unexplored basins.
backlog.title: Basin-signature archive with duplicate skipping

backlog.spec: After each refined packing, identify circles touching at least one wall (within 1e-6). Freeze all interior circles and optimise only the wall circles, each restricted to slide along its wall (one coordinate free), with the radii solved by the exact LP. Use a small SLSQP or bounded 1-D golden-section search per wall circle, cycling through all wall circles twice. Accept the change only if the LP sum increases. This targets the boundary arrangement, which is where the current optimum is least settled.
backlog.title: Rim-only re-optimisation of wall circles

backlog.spec: After construct_packing's annealing loop finishes, spend a fixed last 15 seconds running scipy.optimize.minimize with method='Nelder-Mead' on the 52-dimensional centre vector. The objective is minus the exact LP sum from _score, with centres clipped to [0,1]. Use an initial simplex of scale 0.003, adaptive=True, and maxfev capped so it stops on time. Keep the result only if it beats the incumbent. This is a derivative-free local polish distinct from the earlier pattern search.
backlog.title: Nelder-Mead polish on the LP score in the final budget

backlog.spec: Represent a construction as a permutation of the 26 indices plus a choice per step between grid-hole placement and nearest-free-spot placement. Build each packing by inserting circles in permutation order, each at the grid point with the largest min(distance to others, 2*wall distance), then score by the exact LP. Evolve a population of 20 permutation genomes for a fixed 60 generations with seeded order-crossover and swap mutation, keeping the top 4 as parents. Feed the best genome's packing into the existing refinement. Use a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Genetic programming over greedy insertion orders

backlog.spec: Modify _slsqp_refine to run SLSQP in chunks of 10 iterations (maxiter=10 per call, warm-started from the previous z). Stop when the LP-scored sum improves by less than 1e-7 over two consecutive chunks, or after the original iteration cap. Track the total time spent, and let the basin-hopping loop use the saved time by raising its iteration count for the remaining wall-clock budget. This keeps the refinement quality per candidate while trading time for more candidates.
backlog.title: Early-stop SLSQP with reinvested time

backlog.spec: Build the packing from the bottom up. Start with a fixed-seed 16-circle random layout, optimise it with the existing relax and LP score, then add one circle at a time at the grid point of largest hole size. After each insertion, run a short relax (150 steps) on all circles, then an LP score, until 26 circles are reached. Finally pass the result to the existing SLSQP refinement and the basin-hopping loop. Unlike one-shot insertion, every stage re-optimises the whole configuration.
backlog.title: Bottom-up accretion with full re-optimisation

backlog.spec: Define a robust score as the minimum, over 8 fixed-seed jitter patterns of the centres (Gaussian with sd 0.004, clipped to [0,1]), of the exact LP sum computed on the jittered centres. Use this robust score as the acceptance criterion in the basin-hopping loop and in the final selection, while keeping the unjittered LP for reporting the returned radii. Packings that stay near-feasible and high-scoring under small perturbations are favoured, which may pick basins with more slack.
backlog.title: Worst-case robust objective over centre jitter

backlog.spec: Many basin-hopping moves return the same LP sum to four decimals, so acceptance cannot tell candidates apart. Add a secondary key computed from the same LP solve: the minimum over circles of (LP slack in that circle's wall and pair constraints), or equivalently the sum of squared radii, scaled by 1e-4 so it never overrides a sum difference above 1e-4. Use the composite key (s + 1e-4 * secondary) in the acceptance test and in best-so-far tracking inside construct_packing, while the returned radii still come from the exact LP. Keep the fixed seed and the existing time cut-off.
backlog.title: Lexicographic tie-break score to escape the sum plateau

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that selects all circles within distance 0.12 of any wall (about 10 to 12 circles). Rotate their centres together about the square centre (0.5, 0.5) by a random angle drawn from U[-0.15, 0.15] radians, leaving interior circles fixed. Then run the existing _relax with a small step, _slsqp_refine with 80 iterations and _score. The move slides the boundary ring along the container, a degree of freedom that single-circle kicks rarely reach. Choose this move with probability 0.15 and keep the other moves unchanged.
backlog.title: Rim-ring rotation move

backlog.spec: After _two_phase, run a short stage over the 52-dimensional centre vector. Each iteration draws a fixed-seed random unit direction d in R^52, then runs a golden-section search on alpha in [-0.02, 0.02] for the function f(alpha) = exact LP sum of radii at c + alpha * d (clipped to [0,1]). Keep the best alpha if it improves the score, then re-run _slsqp_refine with 40 iterations on the accepted centres. Stop after a fixed number of directions (about 60) or when the time budget is spent. This is a line-search method, not a pattern search, and it uses no gradients.
backlog.title: Random-direction golden-section line search on the joint centre vector

backlog.spec: Replace the Gaussian centre kick in the basin-hopping loop with a deterministic low-discrepancy sequence. Generate a 2-D Halton sequence (bases 2 and 3) of length 4096 at start-up, map its points to a 2-circle-subset selector and a 2 x k displacement with components in [-1, 1] scaled by the current move size (0.01 to 0.05). Consume the sequence in order so each move uses the next unused point; wrap around when exhausted. The fixed sequence gives even coverage of move space and removes dependence on the RandomState draws. Keep the grid-hole reinsertion move as it is.
backlog.title: Halton low-discrepancy perturbation directions

backlog.spec: Replace the Metropolis-style acceptance in the second construct_packing loop with record-to-record travel. Accept a candidate with LP score s whenever s >= best_s - D(t), where D(t) = 0.004 * (1 - t / T_total) and t is elapsed time since the loop started. Always keep the best-so-far solution separately, and when the current solution drifts more than D(t) below best_s for 40 consecutive moves, reset the current state to the best. This is a threshold acceptance rule with a time-based schedule, not a temperature.
backlog.title: Record-to-record travel acceptance with a linearly shrinking threshold

backlog.spec: Basin hopping currently picks its move type with a fixed coin flip. Define four operators: single-circle grid reinsertion, two-to-four circle Gaussian kick, rim-ring rotation, and large-small swap. Keep a count and a running mean reward for each, where reward is 1 if the move produces a new best-so-far and 0.5 if it is accepted with a score within 1e-6 of the current value. Select operators by UCB1 with exploration constant 0.5 (score = mean + c * sqrt(log(t) / n_i)), trying each operator once first. Use the fixed seed for tie-breaks. The time-based cut-off stays unchanged.
backlog.title: UCB bandit over move operators

backlog.spec: After _two_phase, add a deterministic stage that moves centres to match target pair distances D_ij = r_i + r_j, with r taken from the incumbent LP radii, and a weight of 1 / D_ij^2 on each pair. Run SMACOF (Guttman transform) for 60 iterations, computing the update with numpy, and then clip centres to [0,1]. Feed the result through _slsqp_refine with 60 iterations and _score. Accept the new centres only if their exact LP sum exceeds the incumbent's. This offers a different geometric target from the physics relaxation and the penalty-based methods.
backlog.title: SMACOF stress majorisation toward LP-radius target distances

backlog.spec: Add a fixed-seed particle swarm stage after _two_phase. Use 16 particles whose 52-dimensional positions are initialised as the incumbent centres plus N(0, 0.03) noise, with velocities initialised at zero. Each iteration updates velocity with inertia 0.6, cognitive and social coefficients 1.5 each, and clips positions to [0,1]. Score each particle with _score (exact LP) after a short _relax with 30 steps to resolve overlaps, then keep personal and global bests. Stop at a fixed iteration count (about 40) or when the 60-second budget is spent. Return the global best through _make_valid.
backlog.title: Particle swarm over the centre vector with LP scoring

backlog.spec: The basin-hopping centre kick currently uses one scale for all circles. Change the perturbation so that the Gaussian displacement for circle i has standard deviation proportional to its incumbent radius: sigma_i = k * r_i with k drawn uniformly from [0.2, 0.8] per move. Small circles then move in small steps and large circles move more, which matches the size structure of the packing. Apply this only to the kicked subset and keep the subset size rule and acceptance test unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-scaled kick size in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Keep a memory vector m, initially zero in R^52, of the difference between the last accepted centre set and the one before it. For each new basin-hopping candidate, form the start point c + beta * m with beta = 0.5 and then apply the usual kick and relaxation. After each accepted move, update m = 0.7 * m + (c_new - c_old). Reset m to zero when three consecutive moves are rejected. This carries the successful displacement direction forward, which is different from the one-fifth success rule and from tabu memory, and it adds no extra LP solves.
backlog.title: Heavy-ball momentum over accepted basin-hopping steps

backlog.spec: Replace the linear decay in _relax (decay = 1 - 0.9*k/(steps-1)) with an SGDR-style cosine schedule that restarts 3 times within each relax call, decaying the center and radius step sizes lr_c and lr_r from full to 10% of their value in each cycle. Keep the overlap and wall forces, the template pull and all other arguments unchanged, and use a fixed seed for any randomness. The aim is to let the relaxation escape jammed states it reaches at a single step size.
backlog.title: Cosine warm-restart step schedule in _relax

backlog.spec: After _two_phase, repeat for a fixed number of rounds: draw a random orthogonal 52x52 matrix Q from a fixed-seed QR decomposition, and for each column q_k of Q perform a 1-D golden-section or bracketing search on the exact LP sum (via _score) of centers + t*q_k, with the step bounded so that centers stay in [0,1]. Accept only improvements. This is a derivative-free search along directions that are not aligned with the coordinate axes, so it can move along diagonal contact-chain directions that axis-wise sweeps miss.
backlog.title: Random orthogonal-basis coordinate line search

backlog.spec: In the construct_packing basin-hopping loop, keep a small Pareto archive of accepted packings scored on three objectives: the LP sum of radii, the minimum radius, and the number of contacts within 1e-6 (contact count). A candidate is accepted into the archive if it is non-dominated; the next parent is drawn uniformly from the archive rather than from the single current state. Keep the best-sum packing as the returned answer. Use a fixed seed and cap the archive at 8 members.
backlog.title: Pareto archive for basin-hopping acceptance

backlog.spec: Add a new start generator to the coarse phase of _two_phase: sample 26 fixed-seed random seed points uniformly in the square, compute their Voronoi cells over a 60x60 grid (nearest-seed assignment), and place each circle at the centroid of its cell, then set the initial radii to the distance to the nearest other centroid times 0.5. Use it for every third population member only, leaving the remaining starts unchanged. This gives natural cell-shaped spacing with variable density, which the uniform-random starts do not produce.
backlog.title: Random Voronoi-centroid starts

backlog.spec: Add a stage that searches over the 6 parameters of a 2-D lattice (basis vectors a=(a1,a2) and b=(b1,b2), plus an offset o in [0,1]^2). For each parameter vector, take all lattice points p = o + i*a + j*b (for integer i, j) that lie in [0.05,0.95]^2, keep the 26 points with the largest minimum distance to the square boundary and each other, and score them with _score. Run a fixed-seed Nelder-Mead or random-perturbation search over the 6 parameters for a fixed number of evaluations, then pass the best 26 points into the existing joint SLSQP refinement. Use it as an additional population member.
backlog.title: Parametric lattice-basis search

backlog.spec: After _two_phase, treat f(c) = _score(c) (the exact LP sum with fixed centers) as a function of the 52-D center vector. Estimate its gradient and a low-rank Hessian by central finite differences along a fixed-seed random 8-dimensional subspace per iteration, using the LP dual values for the gradient where available. Take a cubic-regularised Newton step within that subspace, accepting only steps that raise the LP sum after re-scoring. Iterate until the step is rejected 5 times in a row or the time box expires. This second-order local search is different from the first-order sweeps and perturbation moves already present.
backlog.title: Cubic-regularised Newton on the LP value

backlog.spec: Pick the circle with the smallest LP radius after _two_phase. Split its center domain (the square [0,1]^2 restricted to the cell it currently occupies, initially a 0.2-wide box) into a 4x4 set of sub-boxes. For each sub-box, compute an upper bound on the achievable sum by LP with that circle's center relaxed to the sub-box (pair distances replaced by the minimum over the sub-box), and expand only the sub-boxes whose bound exceeds the current best sum. Evaluate the centre of each surviving sub-box with _score and keep the best. Stop after a fixed node budget. This gives a certified local search for the placement of one circle at a time.
backlog.title: Branch-and-bound over one circle's grid cell

backlog.spec: In _relax, precompute for each circle its contact count (number of pairs with gap below 0.02 plus wall contacts) at the start of each call, and scale its center step and radius step by the inverse of that count plus one (a Jacobi preconditioner). Recompute the counts every 25 iterations. Leave the overlap force, the wall force and the schedule as they are. This makes heavily jammed circles move less per iteration, which changes which local jam the relaxation settles into.
backlog.title: Jacobi-preconditioned relaxation steps

backlog.spec: Modify _slsqp_refine so that the pair and wall constraints use an overlap slack eps that starts at 2e-3 and is annealed to 0 over three successive SLSQP solves (eps = 2e-3, 5e-4, 0), each warm-started from the previous solution. Only the final solve uses exact constraints, and _make_valid is still applied before returning. This lets the solver move through configurations that are slightly infeasible at coarse stages, which may help it cross the narrow barriers between neighbouring jammed packings.
backlog.title: Tolerance-continuation of overlap slack in the final SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a move to the basin-hopping loop that uses the LP dual values from the fixed-centre radius LP (shadow prices of the pair constraints). Pick a circle with probability proportional to the sum of the dual prices of its active pair constraints, then move it to the location that maximises its distance to its nearest neighbour among the 40x40 grid points (a grid-hole move weighted by contact stress rather than by grid clearance). Apply this with probability 0.25 and keep the other moves unchanged. Use a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Dual-price-weighted basin move

backlog.spec: After _two_phase, estimate the Hessian of the exact LP score S(c) with respect to the 52 center coordinates by central finite differences (step 1e-4, fixed seed, about 52*2 extra LP calls per estimate). Take the eigenvectors of the 3 most negative eigenvalues and, for each, try steps of +/-0.02 and +/-0.05 along it, followed by _relax with 100 steps and _slsqp_refine with maxiter 60. Accept any move that raises the exact score. Stop when the time budget (about 40 s) is spent. The aim is to leave flat or saddle regions that plain basin hopping cannot leave.
backlog.title: Hessian-curvature saddle escape on the LP score

backlog.spec: Replace the joint SLSQP with a two-block ADMM. Block A holds the centers and is updated by a few projected gradient steps on a quadratic penalty that pulls each pair distance toward a target. Block B holds the radii and is updated by the exact fixed-center LP (_lp_radii). A dual variable per pair and per wall is updated with step rho=1.0 for 40 outer iterations, with a fixed seed. Score the final centers with _score and keep the result only if it beats the incumbent. This is a different decomposition from the joint SLSQP and the penalty methods already tried.
backlog.title: ADMM splitting between centers and radii

backlog.spec: Add a new basin-hopping move. Pick a random circle i and push it to a random grid cell chosen from the 49x49 grid, with the cell's center offset from its old position. Circle i then displaces its nearest neighbour j by the overlap along the line of centers. Circle j displaces its own nearest neighbour, and so on for a chain of at most 4 links, with each displacement scaled by 0.5. Relax with _relax for 150 steps and score with _score. The chain propagates a disturbance through the contact network instead of moving one circle or a random subset. Use it with probability 0.25 inside the existing basin-hopping loop.
backlog.title: Ejection-chain cascade move in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Re-parametrise the packing in terms of a 26x26 Gram-like matrix factored as X X^T with X of size 26x2, which is equivalent to the centers but changes the geometry of the descent. Minimise a penalty on squared pair distances below the target (r_i+r_j)^2 with radii fixed at a common value, using L-BFGS-B on the entries of X with a box of [0,1] on each coordinate. Then increase the target radius by bisection until the penalty cannot be zeroed, using a fixed seed for 12 steps. Pass the resulting centers to _score as the starting point for the existing pipeline. This is a feasibility-bisection route through a factored, rather than direct, coordinate system.
backlog.title: Burer-Monteiro low-rank distance-geometry relaxation

backlog.spec: Maintain a grid archive indexed by three cheap descriptors of each scored packing: the number of wall-touching circles (0 to 26 binned to 6 classes), the number of circles with radius below 0.05 (binned to 4 classes), and the contact count from the LP pair duals (binned to 4 classes). Each cell keeps only its best-scoring packing. In the coarse phase, instead of selecting parents by tournament, sample a parent uniformly from the occupied cells, mutate it with the existing relax-and-SLSQP step, and insert the child into its cell. Keep the global best. The archive forces the search to cover different structural classes rather than one basin family.
backlog.title: MAP-Elites archive over structural descriptors

backlog.spec: Add a coarse-phase population seed. Draw 60 random points in the square, compute their convex hull, and place about 12 of the 26 circles evenly along the hull edges, inset by 0.05 from the boundary. Fill the remaining 14 circles with a fixed-seed uniform draw in the interior. Run _relax with 400 steps using the same parameters as the existing coarse phase, then score with _score. The seed is a boundary-first layout, which differs from the existing edge-biased Beta starts because the boundary positions come from a random convex hull rather than a distribution.
backlog.title: Convex-hull boundary-first start

backlog.spec: Add a coarse-phase population seed built from a sunflower (golden-angle) spiral. Place 26 points at polar radius sqrt((k+0.5)/26) and angle k times the golden angle, then map them affinely into [0.08, 0.92] squared. Give the first 8 points inner radii scaled by 0.6 to create a dense core. Use the result as one population member, relaxed with _relax for 300 steps and scored with _score. This is a rotationally quasi-uniform start that is not based on rows, a lattice, or a ring, so it covers a different part of the start space.
backlog.title: Fibonacci spiral start mapped to the square

backlog.spec: Before each basin-hopping candidate is relaxed and scored, rank a batch of 16 proposed centre perturbations with a cheap surrogate. The surrogate is a ridge regression on random Fourier features of the 52-D centre vector (64 features, bandwidth 0.3). It is fitted on the (centre, LP score) pairs already evaluated in the run, with a fixed seed. Only the top-ranked candidate receives the expensive _relax, _slsqp_refine and _score evaluation. Refit the surrogate after every 10 evaluations. Use the top-ranked candidate on 80 percent of iterations and a random candidate on the remaining 20 percent for exploration.
backlog.title: Random Fourier-feature surrogate for ranking basin moves

backlog.spec: Add a coarse-phase population seed with a self-similar structure. Split the unit square into a 2x2 grid and place one circle at the centre of each quadrant. Recurse into each quadrant with the same rule until 26 centres exist, adding a fixed-seed jitter of 0.01 at each level. Keep the 26 centres whose squared distance to the square's corners is largest. Then relax with _relax for 300 steps and score with _score. The seed is hierarchical and corner-anchored, which the existing grid, lattice and ring starts do not produce.
backlog.title: Recursive corner-subdivision start

backlog.spec: Speed up _score without changing its output. Store the HiGHS basis or the set of active constraints from the last successful _lp_radii solve. For the next call, restrict the pair constraints to the pairs whose centre distance is below 1.15 times the sum of the previous radii plus 0.05, and warm-start from that subset. Re-solve with the full constraint set only if the reduced solution violates any pair constraint by more than 1e-12. The final score must be computed with the full constraint set, so the result stays exact. The freed time is spent on more basin-hopping iterations within the existing time budget.
backlog.title: Warm-started LP scoring with a cached constraint basis

backlog.spec: Inside the second construct_packing loop, add a move with probability 0.15. Take the circle with the smallest LP radius (ties broken by rng) and delete its centre. Pick a large circle (LP radius in the top third) and place two centres at offsets of about 0.5 times its radius along a random direction. This keeps 26 centres while shifting mass from a rattler to a large cell. Run the existing _relax and _slsqp_refine, then accept with the current rule. Use the fixed rng so the run is repeatable.
backlog.title: Clone-and-delete split move in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Before calling _score on a candidate in the basin-hopping loop, compute a fast upper bound on the sum of radii. Use the per-circle wall bound and half the nearest-neighbour distance, summed over circles (a valid bound because each pair needs r_i + r_j <= d_ij). If this bound is below cur_s - 0.002, skip the LP and SLSQP for that candidate. Otherwise run the full pipeline. This spends the wall-clock budget on more plausible moves. Log the skip count only for diagnostics.
backlog.title: Cheap upper-bound early rejection before LP scoring

backlog.spec: After _two_phase, run a short subgradient ascent on the exact LP value V(c) = sum of LP radii. Get the subgradient from the dual variables of the active pair and wall constraints: dV/dc_i is the sum over active pairs of the dual times the unit vector from j to i, plus wall terms. Step with a Polyak-type step (target value = best known sum + 0.001, capped at 0.05 per step), clip centres to [0,1], and keep the best LP-scored iterate. Stop after a fixed number of steps (about 60) so the run is deterministic.
backlog.title: Polyak-step subgradient ascent on the LP value over centres

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move with probability 0.1. Choose a random rotation angle in [0, pi/3) and a random offset from the rng. Generate a hexagonal lattice of spacing about 0.19 rotated and offset that way, then keep the 26 lattice points closest to a randomly chosen sub-window centre. Replace the current centres in that window with these lattice points, and fill the rest from the current packing. Relax with _relax and refine with _slsqp_refine, and accept with the usual rule.
backlog.title: Rotated hexagonal-patch kick in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that picks a random circle touching a wall, using the LP wall-active set, and slides it along that wall to a uniform random coordinate in [0.05, 0.95]. Its other coordinate stays fixed. The move is a large tangential jump, unlike the Gaussian kick. Follow it with _relax at a small step size (0.02) and _slsqp_refine with 80 iterations, then accept under the existing rule. The move is used with probability 0.1.
backlog.title: Wall-slide kick for boundary circles

backlog.spec: Compute the active pair set from the current LP solution, using pairs whose gap is below 1e-6 times scale. Pick one tangent pair at random, and move the two centres apart along their connecting axis by 0.5 times the sum of their radii. Then run _relax with a small step and the existing SLSQP refinement, and accept with the usual rule. This breaks one contact network and lets a different one form, complementing the edge-flip and rigid-cluster moves.
backlog.title: Bond-breaking kick on a tangent contact pair

backlog.spec: In _relax, replace the fixed lr_c with a Barzilai-Borwein step: lr_k = (s.s)/(s.y), where s is the change in centres between iterations and y is the change in the overlap-force field, with a safeguard clipping lr_k to [0.2*lr_c, 5*lr_c]. Keep the existing decay factor and boundary clipping. Use lr_c as the initial step, and fall back to the fixed step if s.y is not positive. This should reach a feasible low-energy state in fewer steps, so more basin-hopping moves fit in the budget.
backlog.title: Barzilai-Borwein step size for the overlap relaxation

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping acceptance test, when the candidate's LP sum is within 1e-6 of the current sum, prefer the candidate with more active contacts (pairs and walls within 1e-7 of tight). Count contacts from the LP solution. A tie that gains contacts is accepted, which drives the search toward more rigid, locally saturated packings. Use this only in the tie band, so the Metropolis rule still governs real changes.
backlog.title: Move acceptance on a contact-count tie-break

backlog.spec: Every 40 non-improving basin-hopping iterations, pick all circles whose LP radius is below 0.5 times the median. Give them new positions drawn stratified in the four quadrants (one per quadrant, rng-seeded), keep the others fixed, and run _relax with a small step plus _slsqp_refine. Keep this new packing only as a candidate in the normal acceptance test, so it can never displace the incumbent without passing it.
backlog.title: Stratified random restart of the rattler set

backlog.spec: Run the basin-hopping loop first with the container shrunk to [0.04, 0.96] squared, using scaled centres and radii, for the first 60% of the time. Then rescale to the unit square and run the normal loop with 0.002 temperature. The shrunken container changes the wall-contact pattern, so this acts as a continuation between basins. Make the rescaling exact so that the final _make_valid runs on the unit square, and keep the best score seen in either stage.
backlog.title: Coarse-to-fine rescaled search on a shrunken container

backlog.spec: Keep the joint SLSQP and the LP scoring, but optimise over u = log(r) (r = exp(u)) and the centres instead of raw radii. Pair constraints become d_ij - exp(u_i) - exp(u_j) >= 0 and wall constraints become x_i - exp(u_i) >= 0 and so on. This keeps radii strictly positive, removes the lower bound from the solver, and changes the curvature the SLSQP sees. Run it from the incumbent for a fixed iteration budget, score the result with _score, and keep it only if the LP sum improves. Use a fixed seed and the existing time guards.
backlog.title: Log-domain reparametrisation of the joint problem

backlog.spec: Replace the free per-circle radii with a smooth radius field r(x, y) = a + b*(x - 0.5)^2 + c*(y - 0.5)^2 + d*(x - 0.5)*(y - 0.5), with 4 global coefficients. Optimise the 52 centre coordinates and the 4 coefficients jointly with a penalty for pair overlaps and wall violations, then run _lp_radii on the final centres to recover exact radii. This is a different parametrisation from the per-circle radii already in the code. Seed it from the best packing in the population and use fixed seeds.
backlog.title: Parametric radius-field ansatz

backlog.spec: After each relaxation step, project the joint vector (centres and radii) onto the feasible set defined by pair and wall constraints using Dykstra's algorithm, which cycles through the constraint half-spaces and keeps a correction vector per constraint. Between projections take a gradient step that increases the sum of radii with a small step size. Iterate for a fixed number of rounds on the incumbent and final-score the projected iterate with the exact LP. This gives a projection-based feasible ascent method that is not a penalty and not an SLSQP solve.
backlog.title: Dykstra alternating projection onto the feasible set

backlog.spec: Given the top five population members, align each pair by solving a linear assignment (scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment) on the centre-distance matrix after a rigid shift that brings their centroids together. Form child centres as the average of the matched coordinates with a random convex weight drawn from a fixed-seed rng. Repair the child with the existing relax and SLSQP steps and accept it into the population if its LP sum beats the worst member. This is a permutation-invariant crossover, unlike the half-plane and Voronoi splits.
backlog.title: Matched-elite averaging crossover

backlog.spec: At the incumbent, estimate the Hessian of the penalty energy (sum of squared pair and wall violations at the current radii) by central finite differences on the 52 centre coordinates. Take the eigenvectors with the smallest non-zero eigenvalues (the soft modes). Basin-hopping moves then displace the centres along a random combination of two or three soft modes with a fixed-seed amplitude, followed by the existing relax, SLSQP and LP scoring. The kick is structured by the geometry of the packing rather than isotropic Gaussian noise.
backlog.title: Hessian soft-mode kicks

backlog.spec: Take the tangent pairs (gap below 1e-6) and wall contacts of the incumbent as a fixed contact graph. Build the rigidity matrix that maps centre and radius changes to changes in tangency distances and wall gaps. Solve for the minimum-norm displacement that makes all contacts tangent while raising the sum of radii, using a least-squares step with a small damping term. Apply the displacement with a step length chosen by backtracking on the exact LP score. This checks whether the incumbent is a true rigid local optimum of its contact topology.
backlog.title: Rigidity-matrix equilibrium on the fixed contact graph

backlog.spec: Fix the centres and treat the radii as a point in a scaled simplex (radii sum to a budget). Run mirror descent with the entropic (exponentiated-gradient) map on the radii, using as the gradient the dual prices of the pair and wall constraints from the LP at the current centres. Renormalise to the feasible budget and project with _make_valid. After a fixed number of steps, alternate with a centre step from the existing relax. Accept the result only if the exact LP sum improves. This is a multiplicative update, not an additive one.
backlog.title: Mirror-descent on the radii simplex with pair duals

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed number of basin-hopping iterations with a deterministic schedule in which the perturbation radius for iteration k is taken from a one-dimensional Sobol-like van der Corput sequence over [0.005, 0.15]. The move type is chosen from the same sequence, so every scale and move type is visited evenly rather than at random. The rest of the loop (relax, SLSQP, LP acceptance) stays unchanged. Use the sequence index as the only source of variation so the run is exactly repeatable.
backlog.title: Sobol-indexed scheduled perturbation budget

backlog.spec: Once per outer cycle, delete the circle with the smallest LP radius, run the existing relax and SLSQP on the remaining 25 circles with the expanded box, then reinsert the removed circle at the centre of the largest hole from the grid search. Score the 26-circle result with the exact LP and accept it if the sum improves. Repeat for a fixed number of cycles. This is a compress-then-reinsert cycle that differs from the single-circle reinsertion move because the whole remaining packing is re-equilibrated each time.
backlog.title: Bold: sacrificial-circle compression cycle

backlog.spec: Add a stage that sets an isotropic pressure on the container. At each step, draw a random box side L slightly larger than the current envelope, apply a fixed-seed Metropolis test on the hard-disk configuration with pressure P, and accept or reject a centre move. Gradually increase P over a fixed schedule while the box shrinks, then finish with the existing SLSQP and exact LP. Unlike the existing compression stage, the pressure is changed at each step by a fixed Boltzmann-style rule, which tests whether a slow pressure ramp reaches a different jammed state.
backlog.title: Bold: random-tiling stochastic pressure bath

incumbent.description: Adds a discrete reinsertion (dislocation-style) move to the basin-hopping loop: with probability 0.5 a random circle is removed and reinserted at the best grid-sampled hole (maximising clearance from other centres and walls, with a small jitter), otherwise the original Gaussian perturbation is used; the usual relax, SLSQP and LP scoring and acceptance are unchanged.

memo:
Helped: search-structure changes. The physics relaxation (slot 0, -1.2801) and the two-phase coarse/refine search (slot 3, -0.3475) gave the big gains. Smaller gains came from the population seed (slot 7, -0.0166), basin-hopping (slot 8, -0.0183) and the reinsertion move (slot 13, -0.0046). The incumbent is -2.6360, which beats the best known 2.635.

Did not help: new starts and seedings (mirror +0.0217, corner star +0.0228, Riesz +0.0209, torus +0.0116), the penalty objective (+0.0170), annealing (+0.0183) and the trust region (+0.0503). Most basin-hopping, polish and search variants returned +0.0000, so this basin looks saturated. Many slots were aborted as duplicates of code already in train.py.

Next: replicate the incumbent once to check noise and the validity margin. Then try a longer time budget (within about 4 minutes) or a different fixed seed. Avoid seeding changes and ideas already in train.py.
